title: Fahrenheit 451
synopsis: Your job is to burn books. You wear a salamander and a number. Tonight, you'll meet a girl named Clarisse who asks if you're happy.

nodes.text: Clarisse walks beside you. She asks questions.

choices.consequence: You commit to “Answer.” The story records the instinct as “Path” and carries it forward.
You let the choice stand. The path shifts almost imperceptibly, marked by one lasting impulse: Wise.

nodes.text: Mildred has the seashells in her ears.

choices.consequence: The choice lands, and the scene changes around it. If it has a name, that name is Care.
“Stop” closes one possibility and opens another. The moment leaves a clear note behind: Honest.

nodes.text: An old woman's house. Books in the attic.

choices.consequence: There is no taking “Try to save them” back. Honor shapes the silence before the next moment arrives.
There is no taking “Burn” back. Job shapes the silence before the next moment arrives.

nodes.text: You walk back toward the ash. People will need words.

choices.consequence: You commit to “Walk.” The story records the instinct as “Path” and carries it forward.

Some endings reveal themselves last.

nodes.text: You become the book inside you. You recite it, slowly, to children. They learn it. They will, in time, recite it to other children.
You and Granger, eventually, write a new book together. It is, mostly, a list of the books that were lost. It becomes the seed of a recovered library.
You stay by the river. You teach the people who pass. You light no fires you don't need. You die very old, with a small book in your hands that nobody burned.
